questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people text instead of talking, and what we lose
How to write and send text messages more quickly
Why teenagers spend too much money on their phones
How modern poets use mobile phones in their work
questions.why: Neil says they'll investigate why people choose to text instead of talk and how it changes how we interact.

questions.q: What happens at the very start of the programme?
options: Neil ignores Georgina to answer a call
Georgina's phone runs out of battery
Georgina is too busy texting to listen to Neil
Neil sends Georgina a funny message
questions.why: Georgina keeps saying 'just a second' because she is texting a friend while Neil tries to talk.

questions.q: Why is texting popular, according to Neil?
options: It is cheaper than phone calls
It is better for older people
It helps people learn to spell
People like to control what they say
questions.why: Neil says the popularity is understandable because people like to be in control of what they say.

questions.q: What point does Professor Sophie Scott make with the phrase “Oh shut up!”?
options: It is always rude, however and wherever you say it
Its meaning depends on tone, which a text can't show
Young people use it far more often than adults do
It sounds much funnier in writing than in speech
questions.why: She says it can be funny or aggressive depending on how it's said, but written down it's just aggressive.

questions.q: Besides intention, what other information does speech give us, according to Georgina?
options: The speaker's age, gender and region
The speaker's job and income
Where the speaker is at that moment
How tired the speaker is
questions.why: She says speech conveys information from the speaker's age and gender to the region they're from.

questions.q: What problem does poet Gary Turk describe?
options: Texts often get sent to the wrong person by mistake
People type too slowly on small phone screens to chat
If a text comes mid-conversation, someone is let down
Phones make it harder for people to meet new friends
questions.why: He says whether you answer the text or keep talking, 'you're going to disappoint somebody.'

questions.q: What does Gary Turk mean when he talks about treading on mines?
options: Using phones while walking is dangerous
Phones can explode if they get too hot
Texting is a safe way to avoid arguments
Phone communication is full of hidden problems
questions.why: Georgina explains that it means a situation full of hidden problems and dangers.

questions.q: Why does Georgina ask Neil if he is “still upset”?
options: He lost the quiz to her earlier in the programme
She ignored him to text her friend at the start
She forgot to reply to the message he sent her
He dropped his phone and broke the screen
questions.why: Neil says it's easy to get annoyed when someone ignores you to text a friend, which Georgina did earlier.
